item.title: Scores killed, Americans among hundreds missing after Nepal flash floods
item.description: Flash floods tore through a valley in Nepal, sweeping away villages and hundreds of tourists, with Americans among the missing, authorities say.

item.title: FDA approves new pancreatic cancer drug that could extend patients' lives
item.description: Patients taking the first-of-a-kind pill, called daraxonrasib, lived for a median of 13.2 months compared with 6.7 months for chemotherapy recipients, studies showed.

item.title: Prince Harry and Meghan arrive back in U.K., BBC News reports
item.description: Prince Harry and Meghan, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, returned to the U.K. from California on Wednesday, six years after their tumultuous departure, the BBC reports.

item.title: How Dolly Parton donated millions of books to children
item.description: Late country superstar Dolly Parton helped millions of children develop a love of reading through her free Imagination Library program. Hardin Engelhardt, chief learning officer at Marbles Kids Museum in Raleigh, North Carolina, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: Doctor explains what FDA'a approval of pancreatic cancer drug could mean for patients
item.description: The FDA has approved a drug that could extend the life of patients with late-stage pancreatic cancer. CBS News' medical correspondent Dr. Céline Gounder has more.

item.title: See which U.S. states are most at risk from Canadian tariffs
item.description: Canadian officials said the tariffs set to be imposed on more than 800 U.S. imports are "strategic" and designed to target some states.

item.title: Meta settles social media addiction suit for up to $17.1 billion
item.description: Meta agreed to pay up to $17.1 billion to settle allegations that its social media platforms are addictive.

item.title: Clinical psychologist explains Lindsay Clancy's postpartum psychosis defense
item.description: Heather Berlin, a neuroscientist, clinical psychologist and clinical professor at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, joins "The Daily Report" to explain the difference between postpartum depression and psychosis and what it means for Lindsay Clancy's murder trial.

item.title: Meta settles in social media addiction case
item.description: Meta, the company behind Facebook and Instagram, agreed to pay billions of dollars and adopt new safety measures, settling claims that its products have harmed American kids. Kelly O'Grady has more.

item.title: Here are the U.S. states that will be hit hardest by Canada's retaliatory tariffs
item.description: Canada is the number one customer for 27 U.S. states' exports. CBS News' Megan Cerullo breaks down what its retaliatory tariffs will mean amid President Trump's trade war.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy trial testimony ends, closing arguments set for Thursday
item.description: Testimony in Lindsay Clancy's trial is finished after jurors in the Massachusetts murder case heard from 85 witnesses.

item.title: Why Dolly Parton is so heavily associated with butterflies
item.description: The growing number of memorials for the late country star Dolly Parton often features butterflies. Tony Dokoupil explains why they are associated together.

item.title: Meta not admitting wrongdoing in $17 billion settlement in social media addiction suit
item.description: Meta has agreed to pay $17 billion to settle claims that its platforms lead to addiction in kids and teens, but is not admitting any wrongdoing despite implementing new safeguards. CNET reporter Katelyn Chedraoui joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: Details on custody battle over Texas surrogacy baby
item.description: A couple from California confronted the surrogate who refused their request for an abortion for the first time Tuesday in a Texas courtroom. They argue she is trying to take away their biological child. Mark Strassmann reports.

item.title: 75% of U.S. adults aren't interested in a foldable Apple device, CNET finds
item.description: Anticipation is building for Apple's annual iPhone launch event in September, where the company is expected to reveal its first foldable phone. Questions remain though on whether consumers will be willing to pay big bucks for this device. CNET senior technology reporter Abrar Al-Heeti joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Trump fights to keep name on Kennedy Center, warning demolition if renovations don't continue
item.description: President Trump's ongoing effort to add his name to the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts took a turn on Tuesday, with the administration warning that if renovation plans are blocked in court, demolition may be the next move. Nancy Cordes reports.

item.title: Heat-fueled wildfires tear through U.S., consuming thousands of acres
item.description: More than 60 million people are under heat alerts from the Gulf Coast to the Pacific. The dangerous heat is fueling a wave of more than 90 wildfires burning across the U.S. Kris Van Cleave reports and Lonnie Quinn has the forecast.

item.title: Fans mourn Dolly Parton at Dollywood in Tennessee
item.description: Thousands buzzed into Dollywood on Wednesday, one day after Dolly Parton's family announced her death at 80 years old. Skyler Henry has more from the theme park she built.

item.title: Latest developments on Nepal flooding disaster
item.description: Dozens of Americans are among the missing in Nepal after sweeping floods destroyed neighborhoods in Nepal. Authorities say at least 150 people are dead and hundreds more are missing. Anna Coren reports.

item.title: NFL ends Pro Bowl after 75 years, will still honor roster at season's end
item.description: In a news release, the NFL said it plans to "elevate" Pro Bowl selections, with no replacement selections.

item.title: Celebrating National Dog Day with Sen. Jim Justice and Babydog
item.description: Wednesday marks National Dog Day, and to celebrate, Republican Sen. Jim Justice of West Virginia joins "The Takeout" with his pup, Babydog, who has become a fixture in the halls of Capitol Hill.

item.title: Trump insists U.S. achieving "very big victory" in war with Iran
item.description: As the Iran war nears the six-month mark, President Trump said he has "no specific timetable" to resume peace talks.

item.title: Trump says he expects big victory in Iran "soon" but is "not in a hurry" to resume negotiations
item.description: President Trump said Wednesday that he is "not in a hurry" to resume negotiations with Iran, despite claiming the war will be over soon. Taurean Small reports.

item.title: Vance says "groceries cost what they cost" in fundraising text
item.description: In a fundraising text for the Republican National Committee, Vice President JD Vance encouraged financially strapped supporters to skip donating, saying, "groceries cost what they cost." Political strategists Kendra Barkoff Lamy and Erin Maguire join with analysis.

item.title: Ross Fire explodes to over 80,000 acres, forces evacuations in North Texas
item.description: The Ross wildfire has burned more than 80,000 acres across Palo Pinto and Jack counties, forcing evacuations, closing roads and disrupting schools.

item.title: Explaining the cultural differences throughout North America and the U.S.
item.description: President Trump's trade feud with Canada is spotlighting the differences between American and Canadian culture. The 2011 book "American Nations" helps explain how some of these tensions came to be and how the rest of North America has influenced the U.S. Author Colin Woodard joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Why Lindsay Clancy wouldn't go free if she's found not guilty
item.description: Closing arguments in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial are set for Thursday. Clancy admitted to killing her children but says she isn't guilty, arguing that postpartum psychosis caused her actions. CBS News legal contributor Caroline Polisi joins with analysis.

item.title: Pentagon upgrades awards of 3 Marines for actions after Abbey Gate attack
item.description: Five years after the attack in Afghanistan that killed 13 service members, the Pentagon upgraded the awards of three Marines who provided care in the wake of the blast.

item.title: 8/26: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: President Trump says Iran war to "continue for as long as necessary"; Sen. Darline Graham prevails in South Carolina Republican Senate primary runoff.

item.title: Boston Scientific says a cyberattack is disrupting its global operations
item.description: Medical device maker said it is working to assess the scope of the attack and business interruption.
